verdicts.reason: A stretches the original strip vertically: about 40px of dead space opens between the headline and the subcopy so they no longer read as a group, the left 250px is empty, and the NEW badge sits off by itself to the right of the CTA. B stacks badge, headline, subcopy and CTA in a sensible reading order, but the badge and CTA are centred at about x=384 while the text is left-aligned at x=143, so the column has no common axis and the right half of the canvas is dead.

A is a clean stacked group (NEW badge, headline, subcopy, Shop Now) that reads top to bottom with good hierarchy, but the left edges are only nearly aligned (badge about 243, text 236, CTA 251) and the right half of the canvas is empty. B is the stretched strip again: a large gap between headline and subcopy, the CTA floats at mid-height on the right, the badge is detached, and the left third is empty.

A suits the 4:1 shape: the headline and subcopy are flush left at a comfortable margin and the CTA sits on the right, so it reads left to right. Its flaws are the NEW badge stranded about 50px right of the CTA and a slightly loose gap between headline and subcopy. B is the same stretched layout as before: the headline and subcopy are split by dead space, the left third is empty, and the badge hangs off the CTA.
